summary: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a bachelor's at Queens' College, Cambridge, and a Ph.D. at SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden. He served as Field Director for the Greater-India Research Committee (~1934–1941).

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. He held posts with the East India Company, served as Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint (1816–1833), and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanscrit (1831–1860).

Horace L. Friess was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and Heidelberg University, later serving at Johns Hopkins University and holding the Buttenwieser Professorship of Human Relations at Columbia (1962–1966).

Horst Lasic specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999, served as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995), and lectured at Vienna in 1999.

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an epigraphist active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India (~1891–1925) and served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).
Hoseok Leigh worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under teacher Ha-u Kim and earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoseong Kim is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo and served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as a professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004) at Koyasan University.

Hoyo Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961). He spent his career at Rissho University as a professor of Buddhist studies (~1977–2004) and dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 1984–1985).
Hozen Seki was a figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and the University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University (1923).

Hsiao-Lan Hu worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Temple University. Hu served as an associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun was a Buddhist studies and religious studies leader. Trained at Tianning Temple and Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute, he founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as its abbot (~1967–1985), and later held professorial posts at Chinese Culture and Tunghai universities.
Hsiu-hui Ji specializes in Buddhist studies. Ji earned a master's degree at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

Hsu Yun was a prominent figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. In 1953, he co-founded the Buddhist Association of China and served as its honorary president.

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin. Lee completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist studies and religious studies master who studied under Chang Chih and Hsu Yun. He founded the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, Buddhist Text Translation Society, and served as Abbot of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas (~1976–1995).
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ohio University (~1972–1973) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1973–2010).

Huai-Chin Nan worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the ROC Military Academy, the University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan, later serving as professor at Chinese Culture University (~1963–1975), National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and studied under Stephen F. Teiser, becoming assistant professor of Chinese religions at Arizona State University (~2007).
